newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-Mains chasing NSW coaching job - paper.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Mains chasing NSW coaching job - paper.

text.p: SYDNEY, June 4 - Former All Black rugby coach Laurie Mains has offered his services to coach the New South Wales Waratahs next year, Sydney's Daily Telegraph newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The paper said Mains was keen to make a return and quoted current Waratahs coach Matt Williams as saying he was "aware of Laurie's interest in coaching NSW".
Mains, who coached the All Blacks for four years, quit at the end of 1995 to continue running his Dunedin building company.

Williams, speaking shortly before his side left Sydney to prepare for Saturday's State of the Union clash with Queensland at Ballymore, told the Daily Telegraph he was not concerned by Mains' interest.
"I'm right as rain ... I've got a rock-solid contract for three years. In fact, we're well down the road planning for next season," he said.
Williams took the Waratahs coaching post after his predecessor Chris Hawkins was sacked mid-way through his contract.
With Williams at the helm this season, the Waratahs have finished ninth in the Super 12.
